1) the liver is the major organ for drug metabolism; 2) OATP transport is the major pathway of drug entry into liver cells; and 3) the key molecular features of a molecule that will determine the extent of its liver uptake by OATP transport are lipophilicity (logD), aqueous solubilility and passive permeability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of orally bioavailable, hepatoselective drugs.
the design of orally bioavailable liver-selective drugs that can be achieved by targeting liver specific OATPs.
the identification of chemical space that can be targeted for liver selective distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

liver targeting is a feasible approach to improve the therapeutic index of drug candidates and can be accomplished by designing compounds with balanced lipophilicities, high aqueous and low passive permeabilities.
the liver selectivity is achieved by a delicate balance of several factors.
the liver-selective compounds are characterized by a balanced lipophilicity profile, high aqueous and lipophilic solubility and a low passive permeability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
liver-selective compounds should be designed to be absorbed, have high hepatic uptake, low passive permeability, low in vivo clearance, high in vitro stability and low in vitro solubility.
a chemical space with a low passive permeability, high solubility, low lipophilicity and high in vitro OATP transport is a good starting point for designing liver-targeted compounds.

the liver-selective compounds have lower lipophilicity and permeability than the non-selective counterparts, and that the liver-selectivity of the compounds can be predicted from their molecular properties and in vitro ADME data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
liver-selective compounds are not only possible, but that there are a number of general structure-lipid solubility-permeability relationships that can guide the design of liver-targeted compounds.
the liver is an attractive target for drug discovery efforts and that it is possible to design liver-targeted drugs using simple structure-activity relationship principles.
liver selectivity is a property that can be designed and optimized using standard medicinal chemistry approaches.
